definitions.explanation: Something that has been decided or set in advance by rules, regulations, or agreement. Used as a modifier before nouns to indicate that something follows an established standard.

examples.japanese: {所定|しょてい}の{用紙|ようし}に{記入|きにゅう}してください。
examples.english: Please fill in the designated form.

examples.japanese: {所定|しょてい}の{手続|てつづ}きを{済|す}ませてから{入場|にゅうじょう}してください。
examples.english: Please complete the required procedures before entering.

examples.japanese: {所定|しょてい}の{位置|いち}に{車|くるま}を{駐車|ちゅうしゃ}しなければ、{罰金|ばっきん}を{取|と}られる。
examples.english: If you don't park your car in the designated spot, you'll be fined.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used as a modifier before a noun ({所定|しょてい}の + noun). Very common in formal and administrative language — forms, procedures, official documents, and regulations. Rarely used in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {所定|しょてい}の{用紙|ようし}: prescribed/designated form
- {所定|しょてい}の{手続|てつづ}き: required procedures
- {所定|しょてい}の{位置|いち}: designated position/location
- {所定|しょてい}の{時間|じかん}: designated time
- {所定|しょてい}の{金額|きんがく}: prescribed amount
